title: THE COUGH THAT FOLLOWED THE BELLS
deck: Forty-one children cough every Sunday night in a mountain town that has spent five weeks blaming its doctors and its church, and nobody has asked which bell, which room, or what changed last winter.
shape: A diagnosis in six scenes: a reframe from address to bed, a test built to lose, a sweep and a ringer and a mother's notebook that each hold part of the answer and a veto, a descent that finds the pressure no one was looking for, and a cohort check, a commissioning peal and a standing rule that keep the result honest.

scenes.title: Forty-One Notebooks
paragraphs: *Children's clinic, Ostrava Vell · Monday, 07:40*
Ostrava Vell was a mountain town of four thousand people, one church with a tower too large for it, and, since the second week of September, forty-one children who coughed in the evenings.
Dr. Ilse Varga had taped her spirometry curves to the examination-room wall, one line to a child. Every line sagged on Sunday night and climbed back by Thursday, forty-one small tides.

**Ilse Varga**  
Cultures, PCR, serology, three rounds. There is nothing in any of them. No virus I know keeps a calendar.
Judit Moravec, who chaired the town council, had come in with her coat on. Father Matej Hroch of St. Wenzel stood by the door with his hands in his sleeves.

**Judit Moravec**  
The council wants the school shut on Wednesday. A closed school is a thing I can actually do. Tell me what else I can do by Wednesday.

**Matej Hroch**  
While you look for something to shut, leave the bells out of it. This town blamed them for the hail and the winter the cows failed. They were innocent every time.
Illuminara stood before the curves, then before the map beside them, where each child was a pin in the street they lived on and the pins thickened toward the church.

**Illuminara**  
Everyone has plotted the children by where they live. Has anyone plotted them by where they sleep?

**Ilse Varga**  
Where they sleep is where they live.

**Illuminara**  
Usually.
Nives Hadzic had come in with her coat still buttoned. She held out a school exercise book, soft at the corners.

**Nives Hadzic**  
Forty-one mothers, forty-one notebooks. I write down every cough, the hour, and where she slept that night. And Lenka does not fit. We are out on Spindle Road, past the cemetery, the farthest house from the tower there is. She coughs on Sundays like the rest of them.

**Ilse Varga**  
I set Lenka aside as an outlier.
Illuminara turned the pages. *Saturday: to Baba's on Cooper's Lane. Sunday: home at five. Sunday night: coughing, two hours.*

**Illuminara**  
Cooper's Lane is right under the tower. Then she is not an outlier. She is the one child you have who proves something. The cough follows the child and not the address, so it is not a street, and probably not a germ going door to door. It is a room she slept in, and the room has a clock.
*The doctors had asked what was in the children. Nobody had asked what was in the rooms.*

**Illuminara**  
Tell me where each of them slept on Saturday night.

scenes.title: Saint's Flour
paragraphs: *St. Wenzel's tower, ringing chamber · Monday, 10:15*
Dana Kral had pulled the bells of St. Wenzel for thirty-eight years, as her husband had before her, and she watched the stranger look at the ropes instead of the bells and made ready to be annoyed.

**Illuminara**  
I have one question, and I think nobody has asked it. Which bell is the heaviest, and when is it rung?

**Dana Kral**  
Everybody asks which is loudest.

**Illuminara**  
I am not asking about loud.

**Dana Kral**  
Old Wenzel, two tonnes and a hundred kilos. Four of us swing him, Sundays and feast days only. The little ones go from the keyboard, and the hour bells strike by the clock every day.

**Matej Hroch**  
There, you see. The hour bells strike every day and nobody coughs on a Tuesday.

**Illuminara**  
I agree. So it is not the bells. It may be one bell, on one day.

She asked for a single stroke of the old bell. Hroch looked a long time at the rope, and allowed exactly one. Dana and three ringers swung Old Wenzel up, and Illuminara went down and stood on the flagstones at the west wall.

The stroke came through the tower like a blow to the bottom of a chair. The tower pressed its weight into the stone, the stone passed it down, and she read where the paths ran. Under the west wall they stopped. There the rock carried nothing and only hung, a long emptiness with a thin roof, and it answered the stroke the way a drumhead answers a palm.
*Something down there rings.*

**Illuminara**  
Under this wall there is a hollow, wide and shallow. When Old Wenzel strikes, its ceiling moves.

**Matej Hroch**  
The tower stands on rock.

**Dana Kral**  
It stands on the lip of the old adit. The miners' air shaft, bricked and boarded before my grandmother's time. Mind the floor by the lectern, it is hollow.
She pushed back her sleeve. Along the dark wool lay a fine white powder, like flour.

**Dana Kral**  
Saint's flour. It comes up between the boards on every feast day. My grandmother said it was Wenzel blessing our hands.

**Illuminara**  
Then it is not new. Something else is.

**Emil Rask**  
I can tell you what is new.
The chimney sweep had come up the stairs behind them with his apprentice and a bag of rods. He was sixty-eight and filled the doorway.

**Emil Rask**  
Last winter's grant. I did sixty-three chimneys for it in the old quarter. New stoves, sealed windows, no draught, less coal. A house with its windows shut drinks from its cellar.

scenes.title: Two Mouths
paragraphs: *Cooper's Lane, cellars of the old quarter · Tuesday, 14:00*
Emil Rask had one rule for entering a cellar and he gave it on every doorstep: the tenant says yes, or the rods stay in the bag.
Eleven of the twelve said yes. Alois Fenner, at number nine, stood in his doorway with his arms folded.

**Alois Fenner**  
My father's cellar and his father's. Nobody counts my air.

**Emil Rask**  
Then I cannot map it, Alois. Not without you.

**Alois Fenner**  
Then don't.
Illuminara could have found the mouth of that cellar in half a minute. She looked at the folded arms and left it unread. The map would have a gap in it.

In Baba Hadzic's cellar the apprentice, Tilo, who was sixteen and had been told to say nothing, held a smoke pencil to the wall by the coal bin. The thread of smoke leaned toward a bricked arch behind it, where the mortar was thin enough to feel a cold breath through.

**Tilo**  
It is pulling in. All of it.
The sweep took the pencil to a grating in the cellar's other wall. The smoke leaned that way too.

**Emil Rask**  
Two mouths. Don't you tell me it is one. The arch feeds this room, and so does the street.

**Illuminara**  
I won't. The street air should be nearly clean and the arch should not, but I cannot claim either until something counts them.
Ilse Varga had arrived with three laser dust counters in a padded case.

**Ilse Varga**  
Nobody says the word silica in my clinic until a counter says particles.

**Illuminara**  
Agreed. Then a test that can lose. Wednesday at three, when no one is baking and no one is at church. Counters in Baba Hadzic's cellar, the school and down the lane. Ten minutes of the small bells. Then Old Wenzel alone, for ten.

**Illuminara**  
If the school's counter climbs with Baba's, the dust is everywhere and I am wrong. If the small bells raise Baba's, it is the tower and not the shaft. If Baba's has not at least quadrupled within twenty minutes of the first stroke, I am wrong a third way.

**Ilse Varga**  
And if you are right, you still do not know what the dust is.

**Illuminara**  
No. That needs a lab.

**Emil Rask**  
And I want the grating counted by itself. A counter in the pipe.

**Illuminara**  
You shall have one.

scenes.title: Wednesday, Out of Season
paragraphs: *St. Wenzel's tower and three cellars · Wednesday, 15:00*
Nobody could order Old Wenzel rung. Four ringers swung him by their own wish or not at all, and the wish was Dana Kral's.

**Dana Kral**  
I will ring him on a Wednesday, which I have never done, for ten minutes, which I have never wanted. One telephone call from the clinic with a child's name in it, and I stop on the spot, whatever is on your counters.

**Matej Hroch**  
And I will stand in my tower and watch you do it.
The mothers had decided that no child should be in the old quarter's cellars that afternoon. Ilse Varga read the counters over the telephone from the clinic.

**Ilse Varga**  
Baseline, all three: Baba Hadzic's twenty-two, the school nineteen, Cooper's Lane twenty-four. Stoves lit, as on any weekday. Small bells, now.
The five small bells chimed for ten minutes, bright and a little silly.

**Ilse Varga**  
Twenty-one. Twenty. Twenty-four. Nothing.

**Illuminara**  
The small ones are innocent. Dana.
Old Wenzel went up from rest and spoke. The note was lower than anything the ear could hold. It lived in the soles of the feet.

**Ilse Varga**  
Minute four. Baba Hadzic's thirty-one. School nineteen.
Between the boards the saint's flour rose in a thin white breath. Dana let the rope settle at ten minutes, as bargained, but the dust in the lane was still on its way, and the counters kept climbing.

**Ilse Varga**  
Minute fourteen. A hundred and ninety. School nineteen. Cooper's Lane a hundred and twelve. The pipe from the street grating, twenty-six.
The arch had fed that cellar nearly nine times its ordinary dust, and the street had hardly stirred it.

**Matej Hroch**  
It may be my tower's own stone. Limestone dusts. Pigeons. I will not be told it is the shaft until somebody looks at the dust itself.

**Illuminara**  
That is the right objection.

**Ilse Varga**  
The tower is limestone, and limestone will not hurt a child's lung. Quartz will. If I find quartz in this, it is not your tower. If I find lime and pigeon, I will tell the council the bells were blamed wrongly again, Father, and I will say it from your pulpit if you let me.

**Matej Hroch**  
I will let you.

scenes.title: One Course of Brick
paragraphs: *The old air shaft and the adit beneath the west wall · Thursday, 06:00*

Hroch had allowed one course of brick to be lifted from the tower floor, and had asked that it be put back. Under it a shaft a metre wide, plastered smooth, fell into the dark. Emil Rask had put a torch on the timbers below.

**Emil Rask**  
That roof has been rotting since my grandfather's day. Anything that goes down there goes on a rope, and I would be burying it.

**Illuminara**  
I do not need the rope. I do need you on the cable, to read me the counter on my lanyard every ten minutes. If the roof comes down, do not dig. Wait. I will be a while, and I will come back.

She went down into a dark that was a kind of information. The gallery ran a hundred and forty metres under Cooper's Lane, its roof lined with lime plaster and sharp white sand that in places had come away from the rock and hung in sheets. On the floor lay three centimetres of dust the colour of flour. Where she stepped it rose and stayed in the air like a held breath.

**Illuminara**  
Eleven hundred where I stand. The arch you smoked is sixty-two metres east. The street grating's branch joins at forty metres and its air is clean, and it carries about a tenth of it, as you said. I will say so at the table.
She took three samples in glass: plaster, floor dust, and a flake of the tower's own limestone. It would have been easy to feel certain. She made herself wait for the lab.
One thing she had not expected: the bell arrived in the gallery as pressure. Every stroke pumped the long tunnel like a bellows, and each pump drove the dust east along the floor toward the arch.

**Illuminara**  
Emil. If you plug that arch, the plug needs a breather: a pipe to the open air, far from any window. Otherwise the bell will press the dust through the old mortar around whatever you build, like water through a sponge.

**Emil Rask**  
That is what a chimney sweep is for, miss. I would have said so in the next minute.

**Illuminara**  
Say it in this one.

**Emil Rask**  
A pipe along the cemetery wall, to a stub chimney above the roofline. Thirty metres. Tilo can lay it by Saturday.

Then she worked. The tunnel was too long and too rotten to save in a morning. She read where the plaster would let go first, under the bell's footprint, and there she sprayed a lime-and-casein binder from the hose Tilo fed down the shaft, a skin that would hold until a proper crew came. Eleven metres. It took four hours.

**Illuminara**  
A hundred and twenty-nine metres remain untouched. The worst of it is covered. It is not all of it. I want that written down.

**Emil Rask**  
It is written.
The lab result reached the clinic on Friday morning.

**Ilse Varga**  
Angular quartz, three to eight microns, in a lime binder. The same as your gallery plaster. No quartz in the tower limestone. No pigeon. Father, your stone is clean.

scenes.title: The Full Peal
paragraphs: *Baba Hadzic's kitchen and the old quarter · Friday, 15:00 to Sunday, 11:00*
On Friday Ilse laid the forty-one cards on Baba Hadzic's kitchen table, and Nives, who had written them, moved them about like a woman dealing patience.

**Ilse Varga**  
Thirty-one of the forty-one slept on Saturday night, or spent Sunday morning, in a room with a mouth to the gallery. Ten did not, and I will not make them fit. Of the fifty-eight in the same classes who do not cough, six were in such rooms: four with grandmothers who air the house all day, and two I cannot explain.

**Illuminara**  
Then what you hold is a strong trigger in the connected rooms. It is not the whole cohort, and it is not a disease.

**Ilse Varga**  
I will say exactly that, and not silicosis, for a child who has coughed five Sundays. And if a Sunday comes when the counters stay low and the coughs come anyway, we begin again, and I tell the council so.

Tilo laid the breather pipe along the cemetery wall on Saturday, and Rask's lime brick went into the arch behind Baba's coal bin. Nobody would sleep in a connected room until the plug had been rung against. By seven the mothers had every child in the schoolhouse hall, and counters stood in six consenting cellars and in the mouth of the new pipe.

**Ilse Varga**  
Forty in any cellar, at any minute of the twenty, and the rope comes down. Nobody sleeps in a connected room on the strength of the minute the bell stops. Wednesday taught us that. The number is mine. The rope is Dana's.

**Dana Kral**  
I will drop it on your number or on my own ears.
Old Wenzel went up at three-quarter swing, to an empty street, for ten minutes. Tilo's smoke pencil leaned along the cemetery wall, up, and out into the dark.

**Ilse Varga**  
Minute ten. Baba Hadzic's twenty-six. The lane twenty-four. The others twenty to twenty-eight. The school nineteen. The stub chimney, six hundred and forty.
The rope had settled at ten, as bargained. Nobody moved. Wednesday's dust had needed four more minutes to cross the lane, and the counters still had ten left to read.

**Ilse Varga**  
Minute fourteen. The highest cellar in the old quarter is thirty-one, at number four. Baba Hadzic's twenty-nine.

**Ilse Varga**  
Minute twenty. Thirty-one has fallen to twenty-seven. Baba's twenty-four. Nothing has touched forty at any minute, and the pipe is still carrying it up and out.

**Emil Rask**  
The dust went where the pipe led. And number nine is not in this book. Alois never said yes, so he goes down as unverified.
Alois Fenner had gone down his own cellar steps with one of Ilse's spare counters, alone, and nobody followed him. He came up after ten minutes and read it aloud to the street, to nobody.

**Alois Fenner**  
Twenty-three.

**Ilse Varga**  
Under forty through the whole window, not only at the stop. Then the children may sleep where they have always slept, and the rule stays on the wall.

The children went to their beds after that, Lenka Hadzic to Baba's, as on every Saturday of her life. On Sunday at eleven Old Wenzel spoke again, and the people in the piazza stopped with their faces lifted, because the old note was in their feet.

**Dana Kral**  
Three-quarter swing, until the gallery is relined. Seventy strokes and not ninety. I will miss the old swing. The bell will not mind.

**Judit Moravec**  
Emil reads the arch counter every second Friday and after every feast. Forty in an occupied cellar and Dana goes to the small bells until Ilse has read it again. The council pays the relining from the amended grant, done by the first of April, before the thaw loads the roof. The school stays open. I would like it minuted that I was told it would.

**Matej Hroch**  
The parish pays for the cap on the shaft. And no stove goes into a house in this town again until Emil has put a smoke pencil to its cellar.
No white breath rose between the boards. Dana looked at her sleeve, clean to the elbow.

**Dana Kral**  
I miss it.

**Illuminara**  
Keep a pinch in a jar. It is a record now, not a blessing.
Ilse took the spirometer to Cooper's Lane that evening and again on Monday at half past seven, and Lenka's line did not sag. She would take it on four more Sundays, with Nives's cards beside it.
Nives opened the exercise book to the last page. She wrote the day, the hour, and under them what she had waited five weeks to write.
*Sunday night: Lenka asleep. No cough.*
Under it, because Ilse had asked for five, she wrote the number *1*.

critic_line: A mountain town keeps its school, its bell and its right to dissent because Illuminara changes the question from where children live to where they sleep, then lets a mother's notebooks, a doctor's counters, a sweep's airflow and a ringer's veto prove the cure.

translation_sl.title: KAŠELJ, KI JE SLEDIL ZVONOVOM
translation_sl.deck: Enainštirideset otrok vsako nedeljo zvečer kašlja v gorskem mestu, ki že pet tednov krivi svoje zdravnike in cerkev, nihče pa ni vprašal, kateri zvon, katera soba ali kaj se je spremenilo prejšnjo zimo.
translation_sl.shape: Diagnoza v šestih prizorih: preusmeritev pogleda z naslova na posteljo, preizkus, zasnovan tako, da lahko izgubi, dimnikar, zvonarka in materin zvezek, od katerih vsak nosi del odgovora in veto, spust, ki odkrije pritisk, ki ga ni nihče iskal, ter preverjanje kohorte, poskusno zvonjenje in stalno pravilo, ki ohranijo rezultat pošten.

scenes.title: Enainštirideset zvezkov
paragraphs: *Otroška klinika, Ostrava Vell · ponedeljek, 07:40*
Ostrava Vell je bilo gorsko mesto s štiri tisoč prebivalci, eno cerkvijo s prevelikim zvonikom in, od drugega tedna septembra, enainštiridesetimi otroki, ki so ob večerih kašljali.

Dr. Ilse Varga je svoje spirometrijske krivulje prilepila na steno ordinacije, po eno črto za vsakega otroka. Vsaka črta se je v nedeljo zvečer povesila in se do četrtka spet dvignila, enainštirideset majhnih plim.

**Ilse Varga**  
Kulture, PCR, serologija, trije krogi. V nobenem ni ničesar. Noben virus, ki ga poznam, se ne ravna po koledarju.
Judit Moravec, predsednica mestnega sveta, je prišla kar v plašču. Oče Matej Hroch iz cerkve sv. Wenzla je stal pri vratih z rokami v rokavih.

**Judit Moravec**  
Svet želi v sredo zapreti šolo. Zaprta šola je nekaj, kar dejansko lahko naredim. Povejte mi, kaj drugega lahko naredim do srede.

**Matej Hroch**  
Ko iščete nekaj, kar bi zaprli, pustite zvonove pri miru. To mesto jih je krivilo za točo in za zimo, ko so krave odpovedale. Vsakič so bili nedolžni.
Illuminara je stopila pred krivulje, nato pred zemljevid ob njih, na katerem je bil vsak otrok bucika v ulici, kjer je živel, bucike pa so se gostile proti cerkvi.

**Illuminara**  
Vsi ste otroke razporedili po kraju, kjer živijo. Jih je kdo razporedil po kraju, kjer spijo?

**Ilse Varga**  
Kjer spijo, tam živijo.

**Illuminara**  
Navadno.
Nives Hadzic je prišla s še vedno zapetim plaščem. Ponudila je šolski zvezek z obrabljenimi vogali.

**Nives Hadzic**  
Enainštirideset mater, enainštirideset zvezkov. Zapišem vsak kašelj, uro in kraj, kjer je tisto noč spala. Lenka pa ne sodi zraven. Smo na Vretenovi cesti, za pokopališčem, v najbolj oddaljeni hiši od zvonika. Ob nedeljah kašlja kakor vsi drugi.

**Ilse Varga**  
Lenko sem izločila kot osamelca.
Illuminara je obračala strani. *Sobota: pri babici v Sodarski ulici. Nedelja: domov ob petih. Nedelja zvečer: kašelj, dve uri.*

**Illuminara**  
Sodarska ulica je tik pod zvonikom. Potem ni osamelec. Je edini otrok, ki ga imate in nekaj dokazuje. Kašelj sledi otroku, ne naslovu, zato ni ulica in verjetno tudi ne klica, ki hodi od vrat do vrat. Gre za sobo, v kateri je spala, ta soba pa ima uro.
*Zdravniki so spraševali, kaj je v otrocih. Nihče ni vprašal, kaj je v sobah.*

**Illuminara**  
Povejte mi, kje je vsak od njih spal v soboto zvečer.

scenes.title: Svetnikova moka
paragraphs: *Zvonik sv. Wenzla, zvonilnica · ponedeljek, 10:15*
Dana Kral je zvonove sv. Wenzla vlekla osemintrideset let, pred njo pa njen mož, in ko je opazovala tujko, ki je gledala vrvi namesto zvonov, se je pripravila, da jo bo razjezila.

**Illuminara**  
Imam eno vprašanje in mislim, da ga ni postavil še nihče. Kateri zvon je najtežji in kdaj zvoni?

**Dana Kral**  
Vsi sprašujejo, kateri je najglasnejši.

**Illuminara**  
Ne sprašujem o glasnosti.

**Dana Kral**  
Stari Wenzel, dve toni in sto kilogramov. Štirje ga zagugamo, samo ob nedeljah in praznikih. Majhni se oglašajo s tipkovnice, urni zvonovi pa vsak dan udarjajo po uri.

**Matej Hroch**  
Vidite. Urni zvonovi udarjajo vsak dan, pa ob torkih nihče ne kašlja.

**Illuminara**  
Strinjam se. Torej ne gre za zvonove. Morda gre za en zvon, enega dne.

Prosila je za en sam udarec starega zvona. Hroch je dolgo gledal vrv in dovolil natanko enega. Dana in trije zvonarji so Starega Wenzla zagugali navzgor, Illuminara pa je šla dol in obstala na kamnitih ploščah ob zahodni steni.

Udarec je šel skozi zvonik kakor sunek v dno stola. Zvonik je svojo težo pritisnil v kamen, kamen jo je poslal navzdol in ona je prebrala, kod tečejo poti. Pod zahodno steno so se ustavile. Tam skala ni nosila ničesar, le visela je, dolga praznina s tankim stropom, in udarcu je odgovorila kakor opna bobna dlani.
*Nekaj tam spodaj zvoni.*

**Illuminara**  
Pod to steno je široka, plitva votlina. Ko Stari Wenzel udari, se njen strop premakne.

**Matej Hroch**  
Zvonik stoji na skali.

**Dana Kral**  
Stoji na robu starega rova. Rudarski zračnik, zazidan in zabit z deskami še pred časom moje babice. Pazite na tla pri govorniškem pultu, votla so.
Potegnila si je rokav nazaj. Na temni volni je ležal droben bel prah, podoben moki.

**Dana Kral**  
Svetnikova moka. Ob vsakem prazniku pride med deskami. Moja babica je pravila, da Wenzel blagoslavlja naše roke.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ni nova. Nekaj drugega je.

**Emil Rask**  
Lahko vam povem, kaj je novo.
Dimnikar je prišel po stopnicah za njimi s svojim vajencem in vrečo palic. Star je bil oseminšestdeset let in zapolnil je vrata.

**Emil Rask**  
Lanskozimska subvencija. Z njo sem v stari četrti uredil triinšestdeset dimnikov. Nove peči, zatesnjena okna, brez prepiha, manj premoga. Hiša z zaprtimi okni pije iz kleti.

scenes.title: Dve ustji
paragraphs: *Sodarska ulica, kleti stare četrti · torek, 14:00*
Emil Rask je imel eno pravilo za vstop v klet in povedal ga je na vsakem pragu: stanovalec reče da ali pa palice ostanejo v vreči.
Enajst od dvanajstih jih je reklo da. Alois Fenner na številki devet je stal na pragu s prekrižanimi rokami.

**Alois Fenner**  
Klet mojega očeta in njegovega očeta. Nihče ne bo štel mojega zraka.

**Emil Rask**  
Potem je ne morem vrisati, Alois. Ne brez vas.

**Alois Fenner**  
Potem je ne.
Illuminara bi ustje te kleti lahko našla v pol minute. Pogledala je prekrižani roki in ga pustila neprebranega. Na zemljevidu bo vrzel.

V kleti Babe Hadzic je šestnajstletni vajenec Tilo, ki so mu naročili, naj ne reče ničesar, držal dimni svinčnik ob steni pri zaboju za premog. Nit dima se je nagnila proti zazidanemu oboku za njim, kjer je bila malta tako tanka, da je bilo skoznjo čutiti hladen dih.

**Tilo**  
Vleče noter. Vsega.
Dimnikar je svinčnik prestavil k rešetki v drugi steni kleti. Dim se je nagnil tudi tja.

**Emil Rask**  
Dve ustji. Nikar mi ne recite, da je samo eno. Obok napaja ta prostor, ulica pa tudi.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bom. Zrak z ulice bi moral biti skoraj čist, iz oboka pa ne, vendar o nobenem ne morem trditi ničesar, dokler ju nekaj ne izmeri.
Ilse Varga je prispela s tremi laserskimi merilniki prahu v oblazinjenem kovčku.

**Ilse Varga**  
V moji kliniki nihče ne izgovori besede silicijev prah, dokler merilnik ne pokaže delcev.

**Illuminara**  
Dogovorjeno. Potem preizkus, ki lahko izgubi. V sredo ob treh, ko nihče ne peče in nikogar ni v cerkvi. Merilniki v kleti Babe Hadzic, v šoli in niže po ulici. Deset minut majhnih zvonov. Nato samo Stari Wenzel, za deset minut.

**Illuminara**  
Če se merilnik v šoli dvigne skupaj z Babinim, je prah povsod in motim se. Če majhni zvonovi dvignejo Babinega, gre za zvonik, ne za rov. Če se Babina vrednost v dvajsetih minutah od prvega udarca ne poveča vsaj za štirikrat, se motim še tretjič.

**Ilse Varga**  
In če imate prav, še vedno ne veste, kaj je ta prah.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Za to potrebujemo laboratorij.

**Emil Rask**  
Rešetko pa hočem meriti ločeno. Merilnik v cevi.

**Illuminara**  
Dobili ga boste.

scenes.title: Sreda izven sezone
paragraphs: *Zvonik sv. Wenzla in tri kleti · sreda, 15:00*
Nihče ni mogel ukazati, naj Stari Wenzel zazvoni. Štirje zvonarji so ga zagugali po lastni volji ali pa sploh ne, odločitev pa je bila Danina.

**Dana Kral**  
Zvonila bom v sredo, česar še nikoli nisem storila, deset minut, česar si še nikoli nisem želela. En telefonski klic s klinike z imenom otroka in pri priči neham, ne glede na to, kaj kažejo vaši merilniki.

**Matej Hroch**  
Jaz pa bom stal v svojem zvoniku in vas pri tem opazoval.
Matere so se odločile, da tisto popoldne noben otrok ne sme biti v kleteh stare četrti. Ilse Varga je po telefonu iz klinike odčitavala merilnike.

**Ilse Varga**  
Izhodišče, vsi trije: pri Babi Hadzic dvaindvajset, šola devetnajst, Sodarska ulica štiriindvajset. Peči gorijo kakor vsak delavnik. Majhni zvonovi, zdaj.
Pet majhnih zvonov je deset minut zvenčalo, svetlo in nekoliko smešno.

**Ilse Varga**  
Enaindvajset. Dvajset. Štiriindvajset. Nič.

**Illuminara**  
Majhni so nedolžni. Dana.
Stari Wenzel se je iz mirovanja dvignil in spregovoril. Ton je bil nižji od vsega, kar bi uho lahko zadržalo. Živel je v podplatih.

**Ilse Varga**  
Četrta minuta. Pri Babi Hadzic enaintrideset. Šola devetnajst.

Med deskami se je svetnikova moka dvignila v tankem belem dihu. Dana je po dogovoru po desetih minutah pustila, da se je vrv umirila, toda prah v ulici je bil še na poti in merilniki so se še naprej dvigali.

**Ilse Varga**  
Štirinajsta minuta. Sto devetdeset. Šola devetnajst. Sodarska ulica sto dvanajst. Cev iz cestne rešetke šestindvajset.
Obok je v tisto klet poslal skoraj devetkrat toliko prahu kot navadno, ulica pa ga je komaj premaknila.

**Matej Hroch**  
Morda je kamen iz mojega zvonika. Apnenec se praši. Golobi. Ne dovolim, da mi kdo reče, da gre za rov, dokler nekdo ne pregleda samega prahu.

**Illuminara**  
To je pravi ugovor.

**Ilse Varga**  
Zvonik je iz apnenca in apnenec ne bo poškodoval otrokovih pljuč. Kremen jih bo. Če v tem najdem kremen, ni iz vašega zvonika. Če najdem apno in golobji prah, bom svetu povedala, da so zvonove spet po krivem obtožili, oče, in povedala bom z vaše prižnice, če mi dovolite.

**Matej Hroch**  
Dovolim.

scenes.title: Ena vrsta opek
paragraphs: *Stari zračnik in rov pod zahodno steno · četrtek, 06:00*

Hroch je dovolil odstraniti eno vrsto opek iz tal zvonika in prosil, naj jih položijo nazaj. Pod njimi se je v temo spuščal meter širok, gladko ometan jašek. Emil Rask je na tramove spodaj položil svetilko.

**Emil Rask**  
Ta strop trohni že od časov mojega deda. Karkoli gre dol, gre na vrvi, jaz pa bi to pokopal.

**Illuminara**  
Vrvi ne potrebujem. Potrebujem pa vas pri kablu, da mi vsakih deset minut odčitate merilnik na vrvici okoli mojega vratu. Če se strop zruši, ne kopljite. Počakajte. Nekaj časa me ne bo, potem pa se vrnem.

Spustila se je v temo, ki je bila nekakšna informacija. Rov je tekel sto štirideset metrov pod Sodarsko ulico, njegov strop pa je bil obložen z apnenim ometom in ostrim belim peskom, ki se je ponekod ločil od skale in visel v ploščah. Na tleh so ležali trije centimetri prahu barve moke. Kjer je stopila, se je dvignil in ostal v zraku kakor zadržan dih.

**Illuminara**  
Tam, kjer stojim, tisoč sto. Obok, ki ste ga zadimili, je dvainšestdeset metrov vzhodno. Veja cestne rešetke se priključi pri štiridesetih metrih, njen zrak je čist in odnese približno desetino prahu, kakor ste rekli. Tako bom povedala tudi za mizo.
V steklo je vzela tri vzorce: omet, prah s tal in luskino apnenca iz samega zvonika. Zlahka bi bila prepričana. Prisilila se je počakati na laboratorij.
Nekaj ni pričakovala: zvon je v rov prihajal kot pritisk. Vsak udarec je dolgi predor napihnil kakor meh in vsak sunek je prah ob tleh potisnil proti vzhodu, k oboku.

**Illuminara**  
Emil. Če zaprete tisti obok, zamašek potrebuje oddušnik: cev na prosto, daleč od vsakega okna. Sicer bo zvon prah potisnil skozi staro malto okoli vsega, kar boste zgradili, kakor vodo skozi gobo.

**Emil Rask**  
Temu je dimnikar namenjen, gospodična. To bi povedal v naslednji minuti.

**Illuminara**  
Povejte v tej.

**Emil Rask**  
Cev ob pokopališkem zidu do nizkega dimnika nad slemenom. Trideset metrov. Tilo jo lahko položi do sobote.

Nato je začela delati. Predor je bil predolg in preveč strohnel, da bi ga lahko rešila v enem jutru. Prebrala je, kje bo omet pod sledjo zvona najprej popustil, in tam iz cevi, ki jo je Tilo podajal po jašku, razpršila apneno-kazeinsko vezivo, kožo, ki bo držala, dokler ne pride prava ekipa. Enajst metrov. Trajalo je štiri ure.

**Illuminara**  
Sto devetindvajset metrov ostaja nedotaknjenih. Najhujši del je prekrit. To ni vse. Hočem, da to zapišete.

**Emil Rask**  
Zapisano je.
Laboratorijski izvid je v petek zjutraj prispel na kliniko.

**Ilse Varga**  
Oglat kremen, tri do osem mikrometrov, v apnenem vezivu. Enak kakor v ometu vašega rova. V apnencu zvonika ni kremena. Tudi golobov ne. Oče, vaš kamen je čist.

scenes.title: Polno zvonjenje
paragraphs: *Kuhinja Babe Hadzic in stara četrt · petek, 15:00, do nedelje, 11:00*
V petek je Ilse na kuhinjsko mizo Babe Hadzic položila enainštirideset kartic, Nives, ki jih je napisala, pa jih je premikala kakor ženska, ki polaga pasjanso.

**Ilse Varga**  
Enaintrideset od enainštiridesetih jih je v soboto zvečer spalo ali v nedeljo zjutraj preživelo čas v sobi z ustjem v rov. Deset jih ni in ne bom jih silila v vzorec. Od oseminpetdesetih otrok v istih razredih, ki ne kašljajo, jih je bilo šest v takšnih sobah: štirje pri babicah, ki ves dan zračijo hišo, dveh pa ne znam pojasniti.

**Illuminara**  
Potem imate močan sprožilec v povezanih sobah. Ni ves razred in ni bolezen.

**Ilse Varga**  
Natanko tako bom rekla, ne pa silikoza, za otroka, ki kašlja pet nedelj. In če pride nedelja, ko merilniki ostanejo nizki, kašelj pa vseeno pride, začnemo znova in to tudi povem svetu.

Tilo je v soboto položil oddušno cev ob pokopališkem zidu, Raskova apnena opeka pa je šla v obok za Babinim zabojem za premog. Nihče ni hotel spati v povezani sobi, dokler zamaška niso preizkusili z zvonjenjem. Do sedmih so matere vse otroke spravile v dvorano šole, merilniki pa so stali v šestih kleteh, katerih stanovalci so privolili, in v ustju nove cevi.

**Ilse Varga**  
Štirideset v katerikoli kleti, v katerikoli minuti od dvajsetih, in vrv gre dol. Nihče ne bo spal v povezani sobi samo na podlagi vrednosti v minuti, ko zvon utihne. Sreda nas je tega naučila. Številka je moja. Vrv je Danina.

**Dana Kral**  
Spustila jo bom zaradi vaše številke ali zaradi svojih ušes.
Stari Wenzel se je deset minut gugal s tremi četrtinami zamaha nad prazno ulico. Tilov dimni svinčnik se je nagnil ob pokopališkem zidu, navzgor in ven v temo.

**Ilse Varga**  
Deseta minuta. Pri Babi Hadzic šestindvajset. Ulica štiriindvajset. Drugi od dvajset do osemindvajset. Šola devetnajst. Nizki dimnik šeststo štirideset.
Vrv se je po dogovoru umirila pri deseti minuti. Nihče se ni premaknil. Sredin prah je potreboval še štiri minute, da je prečkal ulico, merilniki pa so morali odčitavati še deset minut.

**Ilse Varga**  
Štirinajsta minuta. Najvišja vrednost v kleti stare četrti je enaintrideset, na številki štiri. Pri Babi Hadzic devetindvajset.

**Ilse Varga**  
Dvajseta minuta. Enaintrideset je padlo na sedemindvajset. Pri Babi štiriindvajset. V nobeni minuti se nič ni dotaknilo štirideset in cev še vedno nosi prah navzgor in ven.

**Emil Rask**  
Prah je šel tja, kamor ga je vodila cev. Številke devet pa ni v tej knjigi. Alois nikoli ni rekel da, zato ostaja označen kot nepreverjen.
Alois Fenner se je sam spustil po stopnicah svoje kleti z enim od Ilsinih rezervnih merilnikov in nihče mu ni sledil. Po desetih minutah je prišel gor in glasno prebral vrednost ulici, nikomur.

**Alois Fenner**  
Triindvajset.

**Ilse Varga**  
Pod štirideset skozi celotno okno, ne le ob koncu zvonjenja. Potem lahko otroci spijo, kjer so vedno spali, pravilo pa ostane na steni.

Otroci so nato odšli v postelje, Lenka Hadzic k Babi kakor vsako soboto svojega življenja. V nedeljo ob enajstih je Stari Wenzel spet spregovoril in ljudje na trgu so obstali z dvignjenimi obrazi, ker so stari ton čutili v stopalih.

**Dana Kral**  
Tri četrtine zamaha, dokler rov ne bo na novo obložen. Sedemdeset udarcev, ne devetdeset. Pogrešala bom stari zamah. Zvonu bo vseeno.

**Judit Moravec**  
Emil odčita merilnik pri oboku vsak drugi petek in po vsakem prazniku. Štirideset v naseljeni kleti in Dana preide na majhne zvonove, dokler Ilse ne odčita še enkrat. Svet plača novo oblogo iz spremenjene subvencije, končano do prvega aprila, preden odjuga obremeni strop. Šola ostane odprta. Želim, da se zapiše, da so mi rekli, da bo.

**Matej Hroch**  
Župnija plača pokrov na jašku. Nobena peč pa ne pride več v hišo v tem mestu, dokler Emil v njeni kleti ne uporabi dimnega svinčnika.
Med deskami se ni dvignil noben bel dih. Dana je pogledala svoj rokav, čist do komolca.

**Dana Kral**  
Pogrešam jo.

**Illuminara**  
Ščepec shranite v kozarec. Zdaj je zapis, ne blagoslov.
Ilse je tisti večer odnesla spirometer v Sodarsko ulico in nato še v ponedeljek ob pol osmih, Lenkina črta pa se ni povesila. Merila jo bo še štiri nedelje, z Nivesinimi karticami ob njej.
Nives je odprla zvezek na zadnji strani. Zapisala je dan, uro in pod njiju tisto, na kar je čakala pet tednov.
*Nedelja zvečer: Lenka spi. Brez kašlja.*
Pod to je, ker je Ilse prosila za pet meritev, napisala številko *1*.

translation_sl.critic_line: Gorsko mesto ohrani šolo, zvon in pravico do nestrinjanja, ker Illuminara vprašanje, kje otroci živijo, spremeni v vprašanje, kje spijo, nato pa dovoli, da materini zvezki, zdravničini merilniki, dimnikarjev zračni tok in veto zvonarke dokažejo rešitev.

literary_score.method: READER_APPEAL_R1: independent GPT and Claude reader appeal; equal model weights (50/50).
shared_strengths: Fair-play medical mystery with an elegant aha (the 'outlier' who sleeps at Baba's), vivid folklore-turned-evidence, and humane touches (consent, shared authority, honest uncertainty) ending warmly. But the play-script format, dense particle counts and a predictable second test after the solve sap tension. Illuminara stays opaque and the children remain mostly data.

Jasna uganka, prepričljivo skupinsko raziskovanje in skrb za otroke bodo te bralce verjetno obdržali do konca. Zapomnili si bodo preobrat s sobami in zvonom. Ponovljene meritve proti koncu nekoliko upočasnijo zgodbo.
shared_reservations: The town-wide blame in the opening summary and Judit's push to shut the school are only stated, then dissolve in a minuted line; the town's fear never gets a voice. A scene with council or parents pressing to close the school or silence Old Wenzel would test Illuminara's evidence and empathy in dialogue.
Deset otrok ne sodi v razlago z rovom, konec pa pokaže le Lenkin prvi večer brez kašlja. Nadaljnji prizor spremljanja bi lahko pokazal, kako mesto pomaga tudi njim.
